excerpt: ⚠️ This is a record attempt, built on other people's work. It is submitted as PR #406 (code) and PR #407 (runs and logs), and both are in review. It only becomes an official record if the maintainers verify it on their own hardware. All numbers below are from one rented 8×H100 node on runpod.io. Modded-nanogpt is a community speedrun: train a GPT-2-scale language model from scratch on 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs until it reaches a validation loss of 3.28 or lower, as fast as possible. Since 2024, dozens of contributors have taken that run from 45 minutes all the way down to around 30 seconds. Three weeks ago, my second attempt hit 30.67 seconds (#396/#397). Since then, @caraxesml made another big jump with PR #404 — 30.25 seconds on GKE (and 30.05 seconds on our RunPod node). That left the 30-second barrier just 50 milliseconds away. This third attempt stacks cleanly on #404 with +175 net lines across 8 files. Same model, same data, same 1,053 training steps, and the exact same math — just less wasted GPU work. On the same 8×H100 node, it shaves off 145 milliseconds and crosses cleanly under 30 seconds at 29.90 seconds. (Quick note on rules: this is Track 1, the standard from-scratch pretraining ruleset. Separate retrieval-hybrid tracks like #380 reach 5–10 seconds under different rules that allow exact lookups from training data.) Standing on other people's work Almost everything that makes this model fast comes from Keller Jordan (who started the speedrun), @francesco-prignano (PR #393), and @caraxesml (PR #404). Because different cloud clusters run at slightly different speeds (#404 ran 30.25 s on GKE vs 30.05 s on our RunPod node), we timed #404 and our code back-to-back on the exact same machine. Why "same math" can still run faster Modern GPUs are extraordinarily fast at arithmetic, so they often spend their time waiting on memory traffic or tiny setup overheads rather than math.
